title: Why Khareef Bookings Land After Midnight
seoTitle: Why Khareef Bookings Land After Midnight
excerpt: A guest who messages at midnight books whoever answers first. Here's how small Dhofar stays, tours and rentals get their khareef chats ready in a weekend.
seoDescription: Khareef season enquiries from GCC guests peak after 10pm. Here's the weekend checklist small stays, tours and rentals in Dhofar can finish before the rush.

blocks.text: It's half past midnight on a Thursday in August, and a guest in Dubai is comparing three chalets in Mirbat for a khareef weekend. Whoever replies first gets the booking and the deposit. Everyone else finds out only when the family has already checked in somewhere else.
The night shift nobody signed up for

segments.text: Khareef season runs from 21 June to 21 September this year, and the Ministry of Heritage and Tourism has built a programme of roughly 125 cultural, sporting and heritage events across Dhofar around it, preparing to welcome visitor numbers in the hundreds of thousands. For the four room guesthouse in Taqah, the two car rental desk near Salalah, or the guide running the frankincense trail, that season arrives first as a phone that will not stop buzzing.

The buzzing does not stop at six in the evening. Guests scrolling from Dubai, Abu Dhabi or Riyadh compare stays after their own workday ends, often between ten at night and two in the morning. A family business that only checks WhatsApp over breakfast wakes up to find the best rooms, and the best guides, already booked by whoever answered faster.

blocks.text: Why GCC guests book after dark

segments.text: Most khareef visitors are not walking in off the street looking for a room. They are messaging ahead, sometimes days before they travel, and comparing two or three stays on the same evening. The one that replies with a price, a photo and a clear deposit instruction usually wins the booking, regardless of which chalet actually has the better view of the wadi.

There is a trust question layered on top this season. The Ministry has publicly urged visitors to book only licensed tourism establishments during khareef, so more guests now ask for a license number or a clear confirmation before they send a deposit. A slow or vague reply loses the booking twice: once on speed, once on trust.

blocks.text: A guest who messages at midnight books whoever answers first, not whoever has the nicest view.
What a missed midnight message actually costs

segments.text: Run the same math on your own numbers. Count how many messages land after ten at night this week, estimate how many of those you are likely losing to a slower reply, then multiply by your average booking value and the weeks left in the season.

segments.text: None of this needs new software before you even try the basics. A family business can finish this list in a single weekend, before the next surge of khareef messages arrives.

items.text: Put your tourism license number in your WhatsApp Business profile and in your standard reply, guests are asking for it this season
Photos, rates and minimum stay for every room, chalet or tour saved as one catalogue message or a single PDF
One saved reply covering nightly rate, deposit amount and cancellation window, ready in both Arabic and English
Bank transfer or payment link details ready to send the moment a guest confirms
A simple availability chart, even a shared spreadsheet, that you can check in ten seconds flat
One person, even if it is only you, checking messages once between 10pm and 7am through the peak weeks

segments.text: Amal eventually stopped losing the overnight bookings by handing the first reply to a chat tool instead of her own tired eyes at seven the next morning. Chatbot.OM answers the website and WhatsApp through the night, sends the rate card and photos the moment someone asks, and saves the guest's dates and contact as a ready lead, so she wakes up to a booking to confirm instead of a message to regret missing. It follows a voice note in Omani Arabic as easily as a typed English question, which matters when a good share of khareef's late messages arrive as notes rather than text. Fix the basics first: the license line, the deposit note, the saved reply in two languages. Add a chat tool only once those are ready, because it can only send guests what you've already prepared.

blocks.title: Your weekend readiness check
paragraphs: Scroll back through last night's WhatsApp. Count the messages that arrived after 10pm and note how many are still unanswered right now. If it's more than one or two, start with the readiness list above this weekend, before the next surge lands.

items.q: Do guests really book guesthouses over WhatsApp instead of calling?
items.a: During khareef, yes. Most GCC guests compare a few stays in chat before they call anyone, often late at night.

items.q: Should I take a deposit before confirming a khareef booking?
items.a: Most small stays in Dhofar do. It protects both sides against a no show once the season gets busy.

items.q: Does my guesthouse or rental need a license for khareef guests?
items.a: The Ministry of Heritage and Tourism has asked visitors to book only licensed establishments this season, so confirm your status with Dhofar's tourism directorate if you're unsure.

items.q: What if a guest sends a voice note instead of typing?
items.a: Reply the same way you would to text. Chat tools including Chatbot.OM now understand Omani Arabic voice notes directly, so nothing gets lost.

segments.text: Khareef fills Dhofar's small stays, tours and rentals every year, and this year's programme through 21 September gives the readiness list above only a few more weeks of urgency, not less. The businesses that reply at midnight, not just at nine the next morning, are the ones that keep the deposit.
